doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Buying the tenor saxophone
summary: Paying off the clarinet, getting a school tenor as a sophomore, then a $610 Selmer saxophone; Buffalo musicians' club.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: And when did the saxophone come into the picture?

Well once I paid off my clarinet. You know I was a junior in high school by then you understand, and the clarinet, because I started paying for it in the eighth grade, so in the early part of my — I didn’t start even playing the saxophone until I was a sophomore. I’d been playing on these jobs just playing clarinet. I started playing, I had a school horn, a tenor, when I was a sophomore. So then I had a Selmer clarinet so I wanted a Selmer saxophone. A Selmer saxophone in that day and age was $610. So I paid off my clarinet and got another loan for $610 and my payments were $14.75 a month. And I paid that all through my junior year, senior year, and I worked construction after my senior year, that summer. So when I left home in September I paid off my debt for my tenor and that’s how I got my horns.
Did you go to Buffalo to buy —
Yeah I used to go there to see people and do the colored musicians’ club and things when I was a little boy.
Yeah. They still have that there.
